overview: Docket (1932-39) on Japanese cotton manufacturing: industry outlook reports, Commerce's effort to probe secretive wood-based staple-fiber production, sample testing against rayon, and consular studies including McConaughy's 1939 review.

people.name: Edwin L. Neville
people.role: Official responsible for a March 1932 telegram from Japan on the Japanese cotton situation and industry

people.name: Donovan
people.role: Official responsible for several despatches from Kobe concerning artificial cotton and a brochure on cotton in Japan

people.name: Krentz
people.role: Official responsible for a 1934 Kobe despatch transmitting a sample of staple fiber

people.name: Walter P. McConaughy
people.role: U.S. consul at Osaka and author of a 1939 report entitled “Japan Cotton Situation—Review and Outlook”

people.name: A. S. Casal
people.role: Author of the brochure “Twenty-Five Years of Cotton in Japan,” associated with the Kobe firm of F. S. Morse

people.name: F. S. Morse
people.role: Person whose name identified a firm of cotton controllers in Kobe

people.name: Makinson
people.role: Official responsible for detailed reports from Osaka on the cotton situation in Japan

people.name: Veatch
people.role: State Department Economic Adviser associated with information on American cotton in Japan

subfiles.title: Continuation sheet listing McConaughy’s Japan cotton outlook report
subfiles.about: A continuation filing-index sheet records the Agriculture Department’s commendation of Consul Walter P. McConaughy’s September 14 report on Japan’s cotton situation.
subfiles.summary: Docket notes Agriculture found McConaughy's Japan cotton-outlook report especially useful for its annual statement.

subfiles.title: Department of State List of Papers: Cotton Manufacture in Japan
subfiles.about: A two-sheet index describes twelve papers and cross-references concerning Japan’s cotton industry between 1932 and 1939.
subfiles.summary: Docket (1932-39) tracks Japan's cotton situation and Commerce's effort to probe secretive staple-fiber production, including sample testing and Osaka reports culminating in McConaughy's 1939 review.

interest: Shows 1930s US efforts to track Japan's secretive staple-fiber and cotton industries via consular reporting.
